title: Human seeded Evals — Samuel Colvin, Pydantic
talk_summary: Samuel Colvin demos PydanticAI's agent loop, emphasizing type safety for refactorability and using validation errors fed back to the model as a retry mechanism. He also shows observability (Logfire) tracing of agent runs, tool calls, timing, and pricing to debug failures.

takeaways.what_they_do: When structured output fails schema validation, they return the validation error text to the model as a tool response and ask it to fix and retry, rather than failing the run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we will take those validation errors and return them to the model basically as a definition and say please try again

takeaways.what_they_do: Type-safe code lets coding agents run type checkers to 'mark their own homework' and detect their own mistakes before finishing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it can use type safety or running type type checking to get get basically mark its own homework

takeaways.what_they_do: They note the naive agent while-loop has no exit; they terminate on plain-text response, a designated final-result tool, or structured output types.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there is no exit from that loop ... it is not clear when you should exit that loop

takeaways.what_they_do: Instrument agent runs so each model call, tool call, timing, and per-span plus aggregate pricing is visible, then debug failures by inspecting the exact exchange.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we also get pricing on both aggregate across the whole of the trace and individual spans
